newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Costa Rica coffee producers call for minimum price.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica coffee producers call for minimum price.

text.p: The president of Costa Rica's Coffee Institute called Monday for the establishment of a minimum world coffee price to counter speculators in the world market.

If no minimum price is set, "the speculators are going to continue taking advantage" of countries that fix export quotas, said Alonso Lara, speaking at a meeting of the CEV group of Latin American coffee producers in Quito.
"We should not permit our coffee producers to be impoverished. Coffee is fundamental for the maintainence of Costa Rica's political and economic democracy," he said.
"Let's recover control of our destiny. Let's not permit that coffee be sold for less than its cost of production," he added.
Lara said it was vital for major producers Brazil and Colombia to agree on policies to restrict exports and put a brake on speculation.
"Complementary measures are needed. Today we feel that there is no trigger mechanism for the regulation of supply," he said.
Costa Rica believes that the Association of Coffee Producing Countries has the faculties to take any measures to regulate supply, Lara said.
